name: Tinzaparin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Tinzaparin is a low-molecular-weight heparin cleared mainly by the kidneys but with significant non-renal elimination; the Irish label reports no accumulation down to creatinine clearance (CrCl) 20 mL/min. For venous thromboembolism treatment (175 IU/kg once daily) it is not recommended below CrCl 30 mL/min; if used, anti-factor Xa levels guide the dose. It has no current US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Irish summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min).
chip: Treatment dose: not advised if CrCl <30

bands.recommendation: Treatment: 175 anti-Xa IU/kg SC once daily (rounded in 1,000 IU steps) for at least 6 days and until oral anticoagulation is adequate; cancer-associated VTE: 6 months (SmPC).
No dose change at CrCl ≥30 (SmPC). No accumulation seen down to CrCl 20 in older adults.

Not recommended (dose not established). If needed and the benefit outweighs the risk, start with anti-factor Xa (anti-Xa) monitoring 4 to 6 hours after a dose and repeat after 3 to 4 doses (for guidance, 0.5 to 1.5 IU/mL in patients without severe impairment) (SmPC). In adults 70 years and older with kidney impairment, the IRIS trial stopped early for higher mortality with tinzaparin than unfractionated heparin (unexplained; anti-Xa did not accumulate); unfractionated heparin is a reasonable alternative.

hd.text: Circuit anticoagulation (labeled): session of 4 hours or less, 2,000 to 2,500 anti-Xa IU as a bolus at the start of dialysis; session longer than 4 hours, 2,500 IU bolus then 750 IU/hour as a continuous infusion; adjust the bolus in 500 IU steps (usual 2,000 to 4,500 IU) (prophylaxis/hemodialysis SmPC). Treatment doses for VTE are not recommended (CrCl <30); if used, anti-Xa-guided. Half-life about 2.5 hours after an IV bolus in dialysis patients.

pd.text: Treatment doses not recommended (CrCl <30); if used, anti-Xa-guided.

crrt.text: Not recommended at treatment doses; if used, anti-Xa-guided. Unfractionated heparin is usually preferred.

monitoring: Anti-Xa (0.5 to 1.5 IU/mL 4 to 6 hours after dose) if used at CrCl <30. Platelets before and during treatment (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia). Potassium in diabetes, chronic kidney failure and metabolic acidosis (hypoaldosteronism). Neuraxial anesthesia timing (SmPC 4.2, 4.4).
